W7170049804.venue: International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)

W7170079368.title: Comparative Analysis of A* and RRT* Global Path Planning with Pure Pursuit Path Tracking for SLAM-Enabled Mecanum Wheeled Robots
W7170079368.venue: International Conference on Electrical Engineering/Electronics, Computer, Telecommunications and Information Technology (ECTI-CON)
W7170079368.abstract: Autonomous navigation in highly constrained environments remains a critical challenge for mobile robotics, particularly in settings that require omnidirectional maneuverability. This paper presents an integrated navigation framework for Mecanum-wheeled robots utilizing the Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2 Foxy) on the NVIDIA Jetson Xavier platform. We integrate Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) to generate high-fidelity Occupancy Grid Maps and implement two distinct global path planning algorithms: A* (A-Star) and RRT* (Rapidly-exploring Random Tree Star). To mitigate the inherent grid discretization errors of A* and the piecewise-linear artifacts of RRT*, we implemented a Pure Pursuit controller acting as a kinematic filter. This ensures continuous trajectory smoothing and stable path tracking without violating the platform’s holonomic constraints. Real-world experimentation conducted in a controlled laboratory environment indicates that while A* offers superior computational efficiency (averaging 28.1 ms) in low-obstacle settings, RRT* yields superior spatial optimality in high-obstacle scenarios, reducing total path distance by approximately 7.2%. Ultimately, the physical system demonstrates robust trajectory execution, successfully transforming discrete global waypoints into continuous, kinematically feasible curves, validating the efficacy of the proposed ROS 2 architecture for real-time edge computing applications.

W7170118121.title: Operational Knowledge Distillation for Efficient Testing and Enhancement of Autonomous Robotic Systems
W7170118121.abstract: Dans la première partie de cette thèse, nous nous concentrons sur la génération de tests et proposons trois nouvelles approches exploitant les connaissances opérationnelles dans différentes phases du processus de recherche : la génération de la population initiale (RIGAA), l'amélioration de la représentation (RILaST) et la génération de comportements dynamiques valides (Dynasto).Dans la seconde partie, nous nous concentrons sur l'amélioration des systèmes guidée par les tests, en montrant comment des connaissances opérationnelles, telles que des données issues du monde réel, peuvent être combinées avec des tests basés sur la simulation afin d'améliorer les performances réelles des manipulateurs robotiques autonomes.Nous proposons deux approches supplémentaires et les évaluons dans un contexte industriel : l'amélioration du système réel guidée par les défaillances (MARTENS) et la réparation du système tenant compte de l'écart simulation-réalité (STRIM).vii

W7171024790.title: Robust path-tracking controller for autonomous vehicles incorporating neural networks and model predictive control
W7171024790.abstract: This paper proposes a neural-network-assisted model predictive controller for improving the path-tracking performance and lateral stability of autonomous vehicles on low-friction roads. First, phase-plane analysis is performed under various driving conditions and vehicle states to identify the stable region in the phase plane of lateral velocity and yaw rate. The phase-plane analysis results are then used to train a neural network that estimates the admissible yaw-rate range without requiring accurate estimation of lateral velocity or tire slip angle. In addition, a preview-based reference state is generated by accounting for vehicle-speed variations over the model predictive control horizon. A linear time-varying model predictive controller is subsequently formulated using a two-degree-of-freedom linear bicycle model to track the reference state. The yaw-rate bounds predicted by the neural-network-based stable-region estimator are incorporated into the controller as stability constraints. The proposed controller is evaluated through CarSim-MATLAB/Simulink co-simulations under low-friction road conditions. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed controller improves path-tracking accuracy while maintaining the vehicle states within the estimated stable region.

W7171426755.title: Coupled Longitudinal–Lateral Predictive Control for Path Tracking of Articulated Wheel Loaders
W7171426755.venue: International Journal of Control Automation and Systems

W7171813349.title: Outdoor Pedestrian Navigation Using Boundary-Aligned Region and OpenStreetMap
W7171813349.abstract: This paper addresses navigation for autonomous mobile robots operating in outdoor pedestrian environments and proposes a boundary-following navigation method that does not rely on semantic segmentation or prior exploration. The proposed method designates local targets at the edges of the traversable regions detected from local range perception. Consequently, the robot performs boundary-following in pedestrian spaces without explicitly identifying sidewalks. To realize this navigation in real-world environments, we introduce a Boundary-Aligned Region (BAR). The BAR is defined by applying a multi-stage dilation process to an occupancy grid map. This region functions as a geometric bias in local path planning, prioritizing paths aligned with boundaries. As a result, stable boundary-following motion can be maintained even in environments where boundary structures are discontinuous or ambiguous. In addition, heading information derived from OpenStreetMap is incorporated as a directional constraint for local navigation, enabling long-distance navigation without prior exploration. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through experiments conducted in outdoor pedestrian environments.

W7171817771.title: Attention-Based Reinforcement Learning for Context-Aware Path Tracking Control
W7171817771.abstract: Effective path tracking control for autonomous vehicles remains challenging, especially in diverse road geometries and varying vehicle dynamics. Although reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise, typical RL policies still make limited use of temporal context because decisions are conditioned mainly on the current observation, which restricts the modeling of long-range dependencies. We propose an Attention-Based Recurrent Proximal Policy Optimization (AR-PPO) agent for context-aware path tracking. The agent combines Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) with self-attention to construct a weighted representation of the vehicle’s state history, allowing the controller to emphasize the most informative past states when generating actions. We train and evaluate the proposed agent in the CARLA simulator on custom scenarios with varied driving conditions. The results show that AR-PPO achieves higher performance than both RL-based baselines and a classical model-based controller in terms of path tracking accuracy and driving stability. This work highlights the potential of attention mechanisms to improve the closed-loop stability and context-aware decision making of RL-based controllers in autonomous driving.

W7202281912.title: Fuzzy Model Identification and Trajectory Control for Agricultural Tractor Robots: An Optimal Hybrid Methodology
W7202281912.abstract: Autonomous agricultural robots require accurate trajectory tracking to perform precision field operations such as seeding, fertilization, and pruning. Classical kinematic models fail to capture the nonlinear dynamics inherent to real field conditions, limiting the performance of model-based control strategies. This work proposes an optimal hybrid methodology integrating Takagi–Sugeno (T–S) fuzzy model identification and Pure Pursuit (PP) control within a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework for a simulated pruning tractor. Data-driven T–S fuzzy models for incremental displacements MΔx and MΔy are identified using Fuzzy C-Means and parameterized via PSO. These fuzzy models are embedded in a PP feedback control scheme with discrete-time PI velocity and PD steering controllers, whose four gains are tuned by a second PSO instance. The fuzzy models achieve identification Root-Mean-Square Errors (RMSEs) of 10.598 × 10−3 m and 8.125 × 10−3 m. Integrated into the control loop, the system yields a lateral RMSE of 6.6 × 10−3 m on the training path and generalizes effectively across twelve complex agricultural coverage trajectories, maintaining a lateral RMSE below 12 × 10−3 m and heading RMSE under 1 degree. This interpretable, fuzzy rule-based approach provides an accurate and replicable simulation baseline for future experimental implementation on physical platforms.

W7202289040.title: A Singularity-Free Vector-Field-Based Framework for Safe Distributed Motion Coordination of Multirobot Systems
W7202289040.abstract: Guiding vector-field (GVF) methods provide effective solutions for manifold-following problems by generating smooth guidance signals that steer robots toward and navigate desired geometric manifolds. Recent advances in high-dimensional GVF design have successfully eliminated singularities that arise in classical formulations. However, robots must additionally achieve obstacle avoidance, interrobot collision prevention, and cooperative coordination in practical applications. When vector-field composition is introduced, existing GVF-based approaches often fail to preserve the singularity-free property. To address this challenge, a truncated GVF and an obstacle-avoidance vector field are integrated in a high-dimensional space, enabling robots to follow the desired path while simultaneously avoiding obstacles. Based on this formulation, a unified and distributed coordination and safety framework is further developed to enable cooperative motion while simultaneously incorporating obstacle avoidance and interrobot collision prevention. Through the introduction of appropriately designed virtual coordinates, the composite GVF is shown to besystem-level singularity-freein the sense of collective nonvanishing and nonpersistence of individual vector-field zeros. Rigorous theoretical analysis establishes safety under nonconflicting simultaneous safety constraints and proves conditional convergence when the avoidance terms eventually become inactive. Extensive numerical simulations and software-in-the-loop experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed method in both single-robot and multirobot scenarios. In addition, real-world vertical takeoff and landing unmanned aerial vehicle experiments empirically demonstrate the applicability of the proposed approach in realistic flight environments.

W7202359995.title: Guaranteed-Safe Highway Trajectory Planning via Logical Guidance
W7202359995.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Electromechanical Automation (AIEA)
W7202359995.abstract: Trajectory planning for autonomous vehicles must reconcile safety with efficiency, yet existing methods address these goals with different trade-offs: traditional cost-function planners lack formal safety guarantees, while learning-based methods produce behaviors that resist verification. We propose the Logical Guidance Layer (LGL), a component that bridges logical safety reasoning and continuous trajectory planning for highway scenarios. LGL reasons over candidate scenarios via Highway Traffic Scenario Logic (HTSL) with embedded Responsibility-Sensitive Safety (RSS) rules for formal guarantees, evaluates them by a utility function balancing efficiency and temporal consistency, and projects the selected scenario into a guidance region for the trajectory planner. Across two traffic densities, LGL combined with a Lattice planner achieves$\mathbf{1 0 0} \boldsymbol{\%}$collisionfree operation while preserving average speed comparable to that of the unguided Lattice planner.

W7202420694.title: Implementation and Evaluation of Stanley Based Path-Following Controllers for Autonomous Vehicles with Conventional Steering
W7202420694.abstract: The miniAFM is an autonomous test vehicle on a 1:8 scale at DLR. The current path following controller, the geoPFC, was originally developed for an over-actuated vehicle with four independently steerable wheels. However, the miniAFM has conventional front-axle steering. This work implements three Stanley-based controllers and evaluates them against the geoPFC. The variants include the base Stanley, a predictive Stanley with a prediction horizon, and an enhanced Stanley with feedforward control via a kinematic reference model. Simulation tests across three scenarios show that the Predictive Stanley achieves the lowest lateral RMSE, followed by the base Stanley. Robustness tests with increased latency show the base Stanley to be the most robust choice without retuning, whilst the Predictive Stanley performs best after parameter tuning. On the real vehicle, the base Stanley outperforms the geoPFC in terms of lateral RMSE. The results confirm the Stanley-based controllers as promising alternatives to the geoPFC on the miniAFM. The enhanced Stanley requires a more detailed comparison by using a parameter optimization.

W7203735398.title: ROS 2/Gazebo Simulation Study of a Pure Pursuit-Based Path-Following Algorithm Toward Low-Cost Autonomous Tractor Conversion
W7203735398.venue: Gazi Üniversitesi Fen Bilimleri Dergisi Part C Tasarım ve Teknoloji
W7203735398.abstract: This study presents the development and validation of a Pure Pursuit-based path tracking algorithm for the low-cost autonomous conversion of a conventional agricultural tractor, using a two-layer methodology. The kinematic parameters of a mass-produced mid-size agricultural tractor widely used in Türkiye served as the reference. In the first layer, a Python simulation based on the kinematic bicycle model was used for controller design and grid-search parameter optimization (k₁ = 1.3 m, k₂ = 0.7 s). In the second layer, the optimized controller was statistically validated in the ROS 2 Humble / Gazebo Classic 11 full-physics environment under four scenarios, with each of the three disturbance scenarios repeated n = 10 times with independent random seeds. The algorithm incorporates dynamic lookahead distance, gradual headland deceleration, and rate-limited steering control. In the full-physics simulation, the mean straight line cross-track error (CTE) was 0.055 m under ideal conditions, 0.085 ± 0.023 m in the RTK GPS scenario, and 0.446 ± 0.011 m in the standard GPS scenario. A 0.15 s actuator delay produced a statistically significant, but bounded CTE increase under standard GPS conditions (5.6%, p = 0.006). The results suggest that algorithm performance appears to be largely bounded by localization accuracy at low operating speeds, and that RTK-grade positioning provides a basis for precision agriculture applications.

W7203740323.title: Stability Control for Real World Testing in Autonomous Racing
W7203740323.abstract: Controlling an autonomous vehicle at the limits of handling is a challenging task. Due to external influences, such as road conditions or weather, a vehicle can easily become unstable. Since most control algorithms assume stable vehicle behavior, they might fail in these situations. Especially when operating expensive vehicles without a safety driver on board, as in autonomous racing, this poses a significant challenge. To enable safe operation at the vehicle's dynamic limits, we present a comprehensive stability control system that safeguards motion control algorithms in autonomous driving. The proposed system consists of an electronic stability control (ESC), a slip control (SC), and a countersteer system (CS), which collectively adapt steering and brake commands from the motion controller to maintain vehicle stability. We validate our approach through both simulation and experiments on a real-world, full-scale vehicle. The results show that the stability control system maintains vehicle stability in critical situations and extends the operational feasible region. To simplify integration, we provide an open-source implementation at github.com/TUMFTM/tam-stability-control.

W7203855948.title: From Research to Deployment in Autonomous Agricultural Machinery: A Review of Path-Planning Technologies Against a Deployability Assessment Framework
W7203855948.abstract: Global labour shortages in the agricultural sector, combined with diminishing arable land and a growing population, are driving investment in autonomous agricultural machinery. Autonomous systems that can navigate crop environments and perform planting, treatment, and harvesting alongside humans are required, but the gap between published research and commercially deployed systems remains wide across most operational scenarios. Why are agricultural robots still not widely deployed in real farms despite decades of research in autonomous navigation and path planning, and what is preventing full farm autonomy? This paper reviews the principal enabling technologies for autonomous agricultural integration, with a specific focus on path planning as the differentiator between research-stage and deployed systems. Current research in human–robot integration, open-field navigation, row identification and following, crop sensing, and power efficiency is synthesised and evaluated against a deployability criterion. A Deployability Assessment Framework is introduced, comprising structured tables that assign Technology Readiness Levels to twelve path-planning families and benchmark eleven commercial and research platforms against field-validated accuracy data. The analysis shows that point-to-point GNSS navigation has reached TRL 9 with over one million commercial units deployed, vision-based crop row following is at TRL 5–7 depending on crop and season, and whole-farm autonomy with dynamic re-planning is at TRL 3–5. The primary barriers are the absence of standardised evaluation benchmarks, the failure of perception models to generalise across seasons and crop types, and the decoupling of terrain and slip feedback from global path planners. Our review reveals that open-field GNSS navigation is commercially mature, but true whole-farm agricultural autonomy remains unsolved because current systems are not robust enough across seasons, terrain, sensing conditions, and operational transitions.

W7204534783.title: Adapting to unknown environment conditions in autonomous racing competition using Iterative Learning Control
W7204534783.abstract: Scaled-down autonomous racing presents a challenging and highly competitive setting, where achieving minimal lap times requires overcoming a variety of challenges, including the selection of an optimal racing line. In this paper, we address the optimal racing line problem together with environment awareness. We propose an improved racing line encoding technique based on an approximate homeomorphic transformation that maps track segments to unit squares used by an Evolutionary Algorithm. The quality of a candidate racing line is evaluated using a drive simulation based on a single-track vehicle model. Using Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy and isochronal segmentation, our method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. Adaptation to unforeseen environment conditions is achieved through an online Iterative Learning Control paradigm that learns the discrepancy between the planned and realized racing line and accordingly adjusts the control reference of the Pure Pursuit algorithm used for racing line tracking. Our experimental evaluation demonstrates that our algorithm is able to adapt to unknown and spatially varying environment parameters, such as friction, to improve racing performance. We show that using the environment awareness can reduce lap time by an additional 14%.

W7204576661.title: Demo: Deadline-Aware Real-Time Planning on F1TENTH
W7204576661.venue: IEEE International Conference on Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems and Applications (RTCSA)
W7204576661.abstract: We demonstrate a complete, real-time autonomous racing stack that deploys Deadline-Aware Monte Carlo Tree Search (DA-MCTS) on physical F1TENTH hardware powered by an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano. DA-MCTS adapts the risk profile of its sampled actions to the compute budget available at runtime, letting a sampling-based planner meet a hard control deadline on a resource-constrained processor without retuning. On F1TENTH hardware, DA-MCTS computes a racing line online and attains lap times competitive with pure-pursuit and Stanley baselines that require a precomputed reference line. Demo video link: https://youtu.be/vgiwadLAvKs and source code link: https://github.com/scope-lab-vu/RTCSA_Demo_ws.

W7204842498.title: PO-RRT* Path Planning Algorithm for Autonomous Service Robots

W7207725447.title: ACA-LOS: Path-Normal Current-Aware Adaptive Guidance for Coverage-Lane Keeping of Unmanned Surface Vehicles
W7207725447.venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
W7207725447.abstract: To address sustained deviation from coverage lanes when an unmanned surface vehicle (USV) executes a complete boustrophedon coverage path under current disturbances, this study proposes an adaptive current-aware line-of-sight (ACA-LOS) guidance method based on online current estimation. The local current is estimated online from the kinematic velocity relationship between the USV and the surrounding water, and its path-normal component is extracted. The estimated path-normal current is used both to construct a current-compensating heading correction and, together with the cross-track error, to adjust the LOS lookahead distance and generate the desired ACA-LOS heading. Complete-path simulations are conducted under constant, time-varying, and spatially varying currents with different current speeds and directions. Relative to conventional LOS, ACA-LOS reduces the mean cross-track root mean square error (RMSE) by 40.80%, increases the tolerance-band compliance rate (Rb) by 27.48 percentage points, and reduces the cumulative cross-track deviation area (Ad) by 68.68%. ACA-LOS suppresses sustained lane deviation caused by current disturbances and improves lane keeping throughout complete boustrophedon path execution. The method supports the extension of USV operation from single-trajectory tracking to long-duration, continuous coverage execution and provides a reference for unmanned and intelligent waterborne operational equipment.

W7208665100.title: Autonomní řízení monopostu Formula Student v simulátoru
W7208665100.abstract: Tato diplomová práce se zabývá návrhem a implementací autonomního systému řízení monopostu pro soutěž Formula Student Driverless v simulátoru CARLA.Práce nejprve popisuje pravidla soutěže, porovnává dostupné simulátory pro autonomní řízení a analyzuje vlastnosti senzorů relevantních pro detekci kuželů ohraničujících závodní trať.Implementační část pokrývá celý řetězec autonomní pipeline od detekce kuželů v mračnu bodů z LiDARu, přes klasifikaci jejich barvy konvoluční neuronovou sítí, mapování trati metodou Graph SLAM, až po řízení vozidla regulátory Pure Pursuit a Stanley.Systém pracuje ve dvou režimech odpovídajících disciplínám DV Cupu -reaktivním pro první průjezd neznámou tratí a závodním s využitím vytvořené mapy.Funkčnost obou režimů je ověřena na třech testovacích tratích a výsledky jsou porovnány z hlediska času průjezdu i přesnosti sledování trajektorie.Součástí práce je také zhodnocení dosažených výsledků a porovnání s existujícími přístupy v oblasti Formula Student Driverless.

W7208758906.title: High-value multi-vehicle scenario generation for autonomous driving testing using a fine-tuned generative transformer
W7208758906.venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part D Journal of Automobile Engineering
W7208758906.abstract: Rare but high-risk multi-vehicle interactions are essential for evaluating the safety boundaries of autonomous driving systems, yet are difficult to cover efficiently through naturalistic replay, single-agent perturbation or manual parameter combinations. This study develops a high-value multi-vehicle scenario generation framework based on SMART target-domain adaptation. Two representative highway scenarios, constrained cut-in and zipper merge, are mined from highD and exiD using event-triggered rules and converted into a unified multi-agent scene representation. A SMART-based generative Transformer discretizes vehicle motions and road structures into motion and road tokens, is pretrained on WOMD, and is fine-tuned on the mined target-domain samples. During inference, Top-p sampling generates multimodal motion-token sequences, while physical-consistency filtering after continuous trajectory reconstruction rejects or resamples candidates with abnormal acceleration and jerk. Generated scenarios are evaluated across trajectory, scenario and system-response levels through open-loop quality assessment, target-scenario construction and closed-loop validation with an IDM + Pure Pursuit SUT. Compared with CS-LSTM, the proposed method reduces minADE and minFDE by 12.7% and 12.8%, respectively, and improves map compliance to 99.10%. Construction success reaches 42.0% for constrained cut-in and 35.6% for zipper merge. Selected critical scenarios reduce the SUT pass rate from 86.7% to 20.0% and expose collision and motion-paralysis failures. These results demonstrate map-compliant, replay-compatible and testing-oriented high-value interaction scenarios for operational-boundary evaluation and safety validation of autonomous driving systems within the validated highway domains.

W7213433965.title: PLAN-MVP: Planning for Learning-Enabled Autonomous Navigation and Manipulation via Perception
W7213433965.abstract: Autonomous mobile manipulation demands tight integration of perception, reasoning, and control, yet fully end-to-end approaches such as vision-language-action (VLA) models require substantial compute and large training datasets, making real-time deployment impractical. We present PLAN-MVP, a modular hybrid framework that uses a vision-language model as a high-level reasoning brain to interpret natural language instructions and generate structured task plans in a zero-shot manner, while delegating execution to lightweight classical modules for real-time object detection, RGB-D pose estimation, inverse kinematics, and joint-level control. This avoids the need for expensive end-to-end training entirely. We validate key components individually: the RGB-D pipeline achieves approximately 5% position error in simulation, and the IK solver converges reliably with low end-effector error, demonstrating that this hybrid architecture is both interpretable and practical for real-world deployment.

W7213878444.title: Comprehensive performance–reliability analysis of ROS-based local planners
W7213878444.venue: Engineering Science and Technology an International Journal
W7213878444.abstract: In the classical ROS 1 navigation stack, local planners compute velocity commands by using global-plan guidance together with local costmap information, enabling mobile robots to follow planned routes while responding to obstacles, kinematic constraints, and local environmental changes. This study presents a multidimensional performance–reliability analysis of five ROS-based local planners, namely Dynamic Window Approach (DWA), Timed Elastic Band (TEB), Trajectory Rollout, Neo Local Planner, and Hybrid Local Planner. A full-factorial experimental design was conducted with two parameter configurations, four environment categories (empty, static, dynamic, and mixed), and a fixed start–goal pose set. In total, 4000 navigation trials were performed utilizing move_base framework while keeping the global planner, costmaps, robot model, sensors, and simulation infrastructure constant. The evaluation combines performance-oriented indicators, including navigation time, deviation time, executed path length, and average speed, with reliability-related indicators, including static collision rate, dynamic collision rate, local planner failure rate, timeout rate, and successful attempt rate (SAR). In this framework, SAR is used as the empirical task-completion reliability indicator, while the remaining reliability-related indicators characterize different failure modes and safety-related outcomes. The metrics are first normalized according to their desirable directions, and the resulting values are visualized using parallel coordinates plots for joint comparison. The results indicate that no local planner is universally superior across all criteria. Based on the overall SAR across all configuration–environment combinations, Hybrid Local Planner achieved the highest empirical task-completion reliability (69.4%), followed by DWA (55.8%), Trajectory Rollout (38.8%), Neo Local Planner (34.0%), and TEB (25.0%). Although the SAR results provide a compact summary of task-completion reliability, the experimental findings show that local planner selection should consider not only task-completion success, but also failure modes, safety, motion continuity, efficiency, and path-tracking behavior. The proposed framework provides a reproducible basis for multidimensional performance–reliability evaluation.

W7213974566.title: Learning to Tune a Mobile Robot Planner: Hierarchical Architecture and Sim‐to‐Real Transfer
W7213974566.abstract: ABSTRACT Autonomous navigation in complex, unstructured environments poses a significant challenge, with traditional planners lacking adaptability and end‐to‐end learning methods hindered by data dependency or training instability. Learning‐based hybrid methods that automatically tune traditional planner parameters are a promising compromise, but we identify an underlying architectural limitation that contributes to constraining their performance: a low‐frequency, high‐latency control loop. This paper resolves this architectural bottleneck by proposing a multi‐rate, hybrid hierarchical architecture. Our framework explicitly decouples the task into three coordinated loops: a low‐frequency learning‐based tuning loop, a mid‐frequency model‐based planning loop, and a high‐frequency learning‐based control loop. To train the two learning agents, we introduce cyclic co‐training, a structured curriculum that resolves training instability and allows the tuner to learn more aggressive, high‐performance policies. To ensure robust real‐world deployment, we further design a Terrain‐Adaptive Controller that infers latent environment dynamics from its interaction history, bridging the sim‐to‐real gap by ensuring consistent tracking performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. On the BARN benchmark, our method achieves a remarkable score of 0.485 out of 0.500, with an 51.6% improvement over the baseline parameter tuning method. Furthermore, on physical uneven terrains, our approach enhances navigation performance by 58.5% and 38.4% compared to the baseline auto‐tuning methods.

W7213976741.title: Unified Semantic Reasoning and Planning for Autonomous Driving
W7213976741.abstract: The conventional autonomy stack layers separate representations, leaving a vertical gap between high-level semantic reasoning and low-level trajectory generation. This paper closes that gap by carrying a single Triplet Ontological Semantic Model (TOSM) representation across the stack. A standardized high-definition (HD) map is first lifted into a TOSM-based semantic HD map with symbolic, explicit, and implicit attributes. Semantic Web Rule Language (SWRL) rules then infer context-appropriate maneuvers such as yielding, stopping, and lane changing. The inferred state is translated automatically into a Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL) mission plan, and the same representation drives a Gaussian-process factor-graph optimizer that produces a smooth, kinematically feasible trajectory. The optimizer reuses the incremental factor graph of the localization layer, and semantic lane and interaction factors tie the trajectory directly to the map. Reasoning, planning, and optimization therefore share one interpretable representation, and every inferred maneuver remains traceable to the trajectory that realizes it. The rule base is logically consistent and agrees with an independent description-logic reasoner. In a closed-loop drive-along on urban routes, the optimizer tracks the routed lane far more tightly than a diverse set of baselines while remaining smooth and feasible. An open-loop evaluation on real driving data recorded in Busan, Republic of Korea, reproduces this advantage against an untuned continuous-optimization baseline.

W7214091939.title: Route Planning with Reverse Motion for Skid-Steer Differential-Drive Mobile Robot Platforms
W7214091939.abstract: Autonomous waypoint tracking is a fundamental problem in mobile robotics, especially for differential-drive platforms with limited turning capabilities. Classical controllers assume that the robot can always geometrically align with the target. However, this fails in tight configurations where the required turning radius exceeds physical limits. To address this, a reverse-capable planner based on single-goal pursuit is proposed. The system uses a Finite State Machine (FSM) to initiate controlled reverse maneuvers and velocity modulation strategies to protect physical components.

W7214149550.title: Target Point Selection in Path Following: A Review for Autonomous Vehicle Control
W7214149550.abstract: Path following is a critical component of autonomous vehicle navigation, significantly contributing to the vehicle's ability to maintain a desired path. This paper presents a comprehensive study on the design of path following control, which is structured in three parts: tracking errors, target point, controller design. The first part defines the references frames and the procedure for computing tracking errors. Next, a comprehensive review of the most commonly used methods for selecting target points is provided. These methods are studied in open loop by means of an analytical example. The open loop simulation results reveal that some methods can be used for control purposes, others for assessment purposes, some are unsuitable altogether. Building on this review, a proposed algorithm is used to construct four control models in order to design Linear Parameter-Varying (LPV) output feedback controllers. These controllers are simulated in high fidelity simulator. Closedloop results, suggest that all methods have different convergence and tracking behaviors in low and high speeds. The target point can be considered as a design degree of freedom that can enhance or reduce the performance of path following controllers. Finally, this survey serves as a resource for researchers and practitioners looking to design path following controllers for ground vehicles.

W7214305429.title: A Field-Deployable GNSS-based Navigation Stack for Outdoor Mobile Robots
W7214305429.abstract: Outdoor robots require more than an accurate receiver and a path-tracking law: the navigation system must preserve geometric consistency from geographic waypoints to actuator commands, expose measurement validity and timing, and respond to invalid or stale state information. This work presents a ROS~2 navigation stack with interchangeable single-GNSS--IMU and dual-antenna-GNSS localization front ends. Both provide a common local East--North--Up state interface for pure pursuit, virtual-point cross-track PID, finite-horizon nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC), and a segment-dependent hybrid dispatcher. The architecture specifies coordinate conventions, datum initialization, asynchronous state construction, waypoint geometry, controller equations, quality gates, command arbitration, and watchdog behavior. Independent physical field runs collected during 2025 and 2026 grape-vineyard deployments support a balanced evaluation of 800 runs, with 100 runs for each of eight controller--localization combinations on an approximately 199.6-m route. The row-hybrid mode yields the lowest run-averaged post-acquisition mean absolute cross-track error (MAE) in the evaluated dataset: 0.00952~m with single GNSS+IMU and 0.00846~m with dual GNSS. These findings characterize deviations of the recorded positions from the reference route under the evaluated conditions. The open-source navigation software and deployment instructions are available in the https://github.com/YiyuanLinXX/PPBv2/tree/main/PPBv2_Navigation.

W7214982013.title: Path tracking failure analysis of an autoware teaching vehicle in real world environments
W7214982013.abstract: This paper presents a systematic experimental analysis of path tracking failures in an Autoware-based teaching vehicle during turning maneuvers, using RTK-GPS trajectory data from 11 real-world runs. Three categories of failure sources are identified and quantified. Procedural sources (manual initialization inaccuracy) produce a straight-line drift of 5.685 m and a turn entry lateral error of 1.693 m. Environmental sources reveal that left-turn and right-turn curves have nearly identical radii ( \(\approx \) 11 m), but the narrower right-turn exit (4 m vs. 6 m) reduces lateral clearance to 1.1 m. Algorithmic sources show that the Pure Pursuit controller’s fixed lookahead distance (1.5 m) mismatches natural speed variation (7–9 km/h on straights, <3 km/h in curves), causing turn entry lag and 96% error growth. When error exceeds the lookahead distance, the controller enters positive feedback, producing a commanded curvature of 18.116 m \(^{-1}\) —61 times the vehicle’s physical limit (0.297 m \(^{-1}\) )—and the vehicle decelerates from 12.6 km/h to 0. The main contribution is a quantitative demonstration of a deterministic cascading failure chain: localization deviation, lateral error accumulation, lookahead violation, curvature explosion, steering saturation, and velocity collapse. This reveals that Autoware’s failure is not a single-source fault but a system-level coupling failure with positive feedback.

W7215104731.title: Motion Planning and Tracking Control of Unmanned Ground Vehicle Based on 3D Lidar Data
W7215104731.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of path planning and tracking control of the Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) with a special focus on control tracking algorithms. The objectives of the research are the implementation, analysis, and comparison of different control strategies: PID, Stanley and Pure Pursuit. The implementation was carried out using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and the Gazebo simulator on the xMachines x100 UGV robot. Through a series of simulation experiments, the performance of the controllers was evaluated by employing a positioning error metrics, heading error and cross-track error. The obtained results indicated that the PID controller achieves the best performance regarding path tracking accuracy, while the Stanley and Pure Pursuit controllers obtain larger deviations, particularly pronounced in the final movement segment. Although the Stanley controller enabled faster task execution and the Pure Pursuit ensured smoother movement, the PID controller proved to be the most reliable solution. This paper provides a systematic insight into the practical application of these algorithms and guidelines for selecting an adequate controller depending on specific requirements.

W7215690130.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Model Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Path Tracking

W7215838186.title: Input Constrained Planar Path-Following Guidance for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
W7215838186.abstract: This paper addresses the path-following problem of unmanned aerial vehicles under bounded control inputs. The proposed guidance strategy employs nested saturation functions to confine the control inputs within a predefined set, enabling the UAV to converge to the desired path regardless of its initial engagement geometry. The proposed strategy remains applicable to any generic smooth path. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is demonstrated through simulations across various scenarios, including straight-line, circular, and sinusoidal paths.

W7215957685.title: SIMULASI ADAPTIVE PURSUIT ROUTE ALGORITHM (APRA) UNTUK ALGORITMA INTERSEPSI ADAPTIF BERBASIS PREDIKSI DINAMIS UNTUK PERENCANAAN JALUR TARGET BERGERAK DENGAN MANUVER TINGGI
W7215957685.venue: JOURNAL OF SCIENCE AND SOCIAL RESEARCH
W7215957685.abstract: Intercepting a highly maneuvering moving target remains a difficult planning problem because the target may change heading, accelerate, halt, or reverse without warning, while the pursuer only receives noisy position observations. This study proposes the Adaptive Pursuit Route Algorithm (APRA), an interception path-planning method that combines short-horizon target-state estimation, time-to-go aim-point projection, dynamically weighted cost terms, and a bounded residual that is learned online from past prediction errors. APRA is evaluated against three classical pursuit laws-Pure Pursuit, Proportional Navigation (PN), and Augmented PN (APN)-on a physics-based synthetic dataset of 3,200 trajectories spanning eight motion regimes, yielding 12,800 engagements. APRA attains the best result on every metric: an interception rate of 90.91% (95% CI 0.899-0.919), the shortest mean interception time (9.65 s), the lowest mean prediction error (8.73 units), the highest path efficiency (0.798), and the lowest control energy (48,022). One-way ANOVA confirms that the differences in time, energy, and prediction error are statistically significant (p < 0.001), and a Welch t-test shows APRA is significantly faster than APN (t = -14.48, p < 0.001). The results indicate that disciplined filtering combined with bounded online adaptation is more robust against deceptive and abrupt maneuvers than raw lead-based guidance.

W7220364781.title: Safety-Oriented Comparative Assessment of Autonomous Path-Tracking Controllers Using a Real-World-Validated Virtual Vehicle Model
W7220364781.abstract: Comparisons of path-tracking controllers based mainly on tracking error may overlook differences in steering activity, vehicle response, and lane containment. This study compares Pure Pursuit, Stanley, and Model Predictive Control using a common virtual vehicle model and multiple safety-related performance indicators. The virtual vehicle model was evaluated against two separate CAN recordings from the same vehicle without recalibration between evaluations. Vehicle-speed and front-wheel-speed predictions showed R2 values above 0.97 in both recordings; yaw-rate R2 values were 0.957 and 0.930, whereas lateral-acceleration agreement was lower, particularly in the second recording. A Common Path Manager provided consistent reference-path information and steering constraints for all three controllers. They were evaluated at 5 and 10 km/h on idealized hairpin and spiral paths using tracking errors, steering-command-rate RMS, kinematic-response measures, and center-of-gravity-based and sampled vehicle-body lane-containment measures. MPC achieved the lowest cross-track-error RMSE in both scenarios, whereas Pure Pursuit produced the lowest steering-command-rate, lateral-acceleration, and yaw-rate RMS values. Stanley achieved the lowest heading-error RMSE in the spiral scenario. In the hairpin tests, the vehicle center of gravity remained within the lane for all controllers, although the body was partially outside the modeled lane corridor in 37.048–53.352% of evaluated samples. These findings show that lower tracking error does not necessarily coincide with lower steering-command activity or improved CG-based lane keeping. The evaluated quantities are safety-related performance indicators for the investigated simulation conditions and do not constitute a comprehensive assessment of vehicle safety.

W7220672305.title: A Flexible and Energy Efficient Wheeled-Legged Robot for Performing Delivery Tasks on Challenging Terrains
W7220672305.venue: IEEE International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE)
W7220672305.abstract: Logistics tasks in sectors such as agriculture and construction often require transporting objects across environments with uneven terrain and obstacles. Although legged robots provide mobility on challenging terrain, their locomotion can be inefficient on flat surfaces where wheeled robots are more suitable. In this work, we present a new platform based on the Dual-Diablo design, a cooperative wheel-legged robotic system designed for flexible and energy-efficient delivery in challenging environments. The system combines two biped-wheeled robots with a rigid tray to transport payloads while enabling multiple locomotion strategies, including wheeled driving, legged walking, and body height adjustment to traverse obstacles. We implement coordinated locomotion gaits that allow the robots to operate together while maintaining payload stability. In addition, we derive a data-driven power consumption model that predicts energy usage as a function of robot velocity, terrain slope, payload mass, and body configuration. This allows the system to utilize the right gait based on the terrain. The proposed design and power model are validated through simulation and laboratory experiments, demonstrating the feasibility of the system for flexible and energy-efficient logistics operations in environments containing traversable obstacles.

W7220861921.title: Notice of Removal: Real-Time Nonlinear Model Predictive Contouring Control for Autonomous Navigation in Complex Urban Geometries
W7220861921.venue: International Conference on Robotics and Automation Sciences (ICRAS)

W7221470012.title: Safe and Energy-Efficient Control Allocation for Multi-Unit Heavy Vehicles
W7221470012.abstract: Electrification, increased variation, and the complexity of multi-unit vehicle combinations have created a need for novel control allocation strategies. Traditional vehicle combinations are propelled solely by the towing vehicle—trucks or tractors—with braking forces distributed in proportion to the axle loads, which is commonly the safest approach. Conversely, modern combinations may be propelled by multiple units, with regenerative braking performed by various electrified units, not necessarily in proportion to the axle loads. An optimal approach for allocating propulsion and braking forces among vehicle units is power loss minimization. This thesis presents a hierarchical, distributed control architecture that effectively manages over-actuation by decoupling upper-level combination control from lower-level unit control. This distributed framework minimizes power losses across multiple units, demonstrating that selectively disengaging electric motors reduces overall energy consumption, while integrating state-of-charge control ensures equal depletion rates among batteries across units in an energy-efficient manner.From an energy-efficiency perspective, concentrating propulsion or regenerative braking on a single vehicle unit may be optimal. However, such allocations can compromise safety by inducing motion instabilities, such as jackknifing and trailer swing. Consequently, ensuring combination stability while allocating unit forces efficiently is essential. This thesis introduces safe operating envelopes for vehicle combinations in both the force and slip domains. Using single-track, two-track, and high-fidelity models, along with phase-portrait analyses, this work systematically establishes adaptive slip limits and safe force boundaries. These envelopes are tested in simulations and real-world vehicle tests, confirming their effectiveness in preventing yaw instabilities. Furthermore, predictive safety barriers—ranging from advanced Model Predictive Control formulations to simpler proportional-heuristic controllers—are developed and tested in simulations, demonstrating promising performance in proactively avoiding yaw instabilities.Finally, this study compares the evaluated controllers and details the envisioned functional architecture and signal interfaces, establishing a robust foundation for the safe and efficient operation of future multi-unit electrified heavy vehicles.

W7221539346.title: Six Wheel Drive Autonomous Precision Agriculture Rover
W7221539346.venue: International Conference on Computer, Mechatronics, Robotics & Artificial Intelligence (ICCMRAI)
W7221539346.abstract: Physical field deployment of autonomous agricultural robots demands extensive hardware validation that is both costly and weather-dependent. This paper presents a MATLAB/Python-based kinematic simulation framework for the SAARTHI six-wheel-drive (6WD) precision-agriculture rover, enabling complete navigation-algorithm validation prior to hardware commitment. All rover parameters are derived directly from the embedded firmware source code: wheelbase 0.42m, track 0.285m, wheel radius 0.05m, and maximum steering angle 27° (0.471rad). Four experiments are conducted: (i) Pure Pursuit boustrophedon trajectory tracking over a three-row 50m×1.0m field achieving 0.28m mean lateral accuracy (σ=0.16m, RMSE 0.19m); (ii) 90° end-of-row turn analysis across four look-ahead configurations, showing that an adaptive look-ahead reduces peak deviation from 0.52m to 0.25m; (iii) Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) localization under GPS (2.5m CEP), IMU (0.028°/s drift), and wheel-odometry noise reproducing crop-type-specific RMSE values of 0.17m (wheat), 0.24m (sugarcane), and 0.28m (fallow), with a complementary filter reducing IMU heading drift by 65%; and (iv) Ackermann 4WS steering geometry validation confirming the ICR stability band of ±0.12m and Mecanum wheel-velocity correctness from the 6×3 kinematic Jacobian. Simulated results lie within 15% of published 12-trial hardware field measurements, validating the framework as a low-cost pre-deployment algorithm design tool for smallholder precision agriculture.

W7221677358.title: Design and Testing of an Autonomous Laser Weeding Robot with Cross-Modal Vibration Prediction for Cotton Fields
W7221677358.abstract: Laser weeding is a non-chemical, non-contact precision weeding method particularly suited for inter-row operations during the crop seedling stage. However, maintaining precise laser targeting on weed stems during dynamic field operation remains challenging. This task requires close coordination among perception, control, and actuation modules, while vehicle vibration from uneven terrain further degrades strike precision on the move. This paper presents a fully autonomous laser weeding robot for inter-row operation in cotton seedling fields, integrating weeding control, automatic mode switching, and autonomous navigation into a coordinated multi-process architecture. Vibration-induced strike deviation is mitigated by STCF-Net (Spatio-Temporal Cross-modal Fusion Network), a cross-modal prediction framework that fuses forward-looking depth maps with historical IMU signals to forecast vibration severity over a 3 s horizon. The prediction enables the control system to proactively adjust travel speed and weeding mode before encountering rough terrain, balancing precision and efficiency under dynamic field conditions. Field experiments validated weeding performance in static and dynamic scenarios and demonstrated that STCF-Net-guided predictive switching reduced operational time by 11.5% to 13.9% compared with a conservative baseline in two controlled experiments, with only a marginal reduction in weeding precision. This study reports the system-level design of a fully autonomous laser weeding robot and introduces feedforward vibration prediction to the laser weeding domain, providing a practical reference for integrating predictive algorithms into field-deployable weeding systems.

W7221700870.title: MSTR-PPO: A Multi-Scale Temporal Residual PPO Controller for Freeze-Prone Indoor Navigation
W7221700870.abstract: Abstract Local navigation controllers often stop making progress in constrained indoor environments, where narrow geometry and moving obstacles compress the feasible motion space until the robot stalls and falls back on repeated recovery behaviors. We treat such freezing as a failure of local control arising from three observable mechanisms, and pair each with one module: insufficient path horizon with a Multi-Scale Path Transformer, motion ambiguity in single-frame sensing with a First-Order Temporal High-Pass Filter, and unstable learned velocity commands with a Bounded Residual Action, reporting empirical evidence that associates each module with the corresponding condition. The resulting controller, MSTR-PPO, learns only a bounded correction around a Pure Pursuit nominal action, so it drops into the standard sensor–path–velocity-command interface instead of replacing it with an unconstrained end-to-end policy. We compare eight learned local-control configurations alongside three classical baselines across nine Gazebo worlds with dynamic obstacles, using three independent training seeds for each learned controller, and deploy the trained policy as a ROS 2 Nav2 C++ controller. MSTR-PPO clears both freeze-prone worlds with essentially no stack-level recoveries, where the best default-parameter classical baseline does not, and attains 92.1 ± 1.3% average success on the main seven-world suite—the highest of all learned variants—at real-time CPU control rates. Stress tests expose a limitation on continuous-curvature paths, and a preliminary Unitree Go2 test transfers successfully at the same interface.

W7222636847.title: VICONav: Vectorized Isaac Configurable Object Navigation Benchmark
W7222636847.abstract: Abstract This paper introduces VICONav, a vectorized configurable object-navigation benchmark for mobile robots in Isaac Lab. The benchmark is built on Isaac Sim and uses USD (Universal Scene Description) assets, physically simulated robot motion, and rendered indoor scenes executed in parallel environment instances. All instances share a common potential object pool, while each reset independently samples the target object, object arrangement, obstacle configuration, and initial robot state. The tensor shapes and object indices remain fixed across episodes, which supports efficient vectorized training and direct comparison of policies under a stable observation interface. Scene generation is specified by a two-level configuration scheme. The first level defines object classes, physical parameters, USD assets, and semantic object tags. The second level defines compositional scene blocks that represent functional zones and object groups. This design separates the object vocabulary from the spatial organization of the scene and allows controlled variation of object composition, target distribution, graph construction, observation modality, and action parameterization. VICONav supports discrete and continuous control, visual and graph-based observations, curriculum-dependent initial-state distributions, and simulator-state access for reward computation and auxiliary training objectives. We evaluate the benchmark through a series of experiments covering learned navigation policies, classical reference methods, and robustness tests under controlled visual and graph perturbations. The results show that VICONav can be used as a configuration-driven experimental substrate for comparing object-goal navigation approaches under controlled changes of scene structure, observation composition, and control interface.

W7222931553.title: Foundation-Model-Driven 3D Scene Graphs for Mobile Manipulation
W7222931553.abstract: Geometric and Semantic Foundation models are becoming increasingly popular tools for generating spatial maps for robots. Recent work (e.g., FOUND-IT) has leveraged these tools to construct real-time, task-driven, and open-set 3D scene graphs from a single uncalibrated camera. However, while classical robot mapping techniques have undergone extensive system demonstrations, limited work has been done to develop both the fundamental and the systems wide advancements needed to integrate these new types of robot spatial memory into a full, useable autonomy pipeline. In this paper, we bridge this gap, and in doing so we also evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of this type of 3D memory. Towards this end, we integrate FOUND-IT into a mobile manipulator platform and demonstrate it is well-suited to support multiple objectives such as object change detection, support for multiple mapping sessions, determination of navigable paths, and directly support object grasping for the task of scene re-arrangement. Furthermore, we provide nuanced insights into the effectiveness and limitations of a monocular, foundation-model-driven 3D scene graph construction system using observations from rigorous on-robot experiments. Code is available at https://github. com/MIT-SPARK/FOUND-IT.

W7222993268.title: Multi-Agent System for Building a Shared Obstacle Map for Autonomous Transport on Enterprise Territories
W7222993268.venue: International Ural Conference on Electrical Power Engineering (UralCon)
W7222993268.abstract: The article considers a subsystem for collaborative obstacle mapping for a group of unmanned motor vehicles operating on restricted enterprise territories. Such territories are characterized by repeated routes, technological passages, temporary obstacles, warehouse infrastructure and areas with limited visibility. The proposed approach combines local dynamic maps formed by each agent from LiDAR data and external odometry with a shared persistent obstacle map in the world coordinate system. Local maps are used for operational planning, while the shared map preserves information obtained by different agents and makes it available for subsequent movement along enterprise routes. The approach takes into account safety requirements for driverless industrial trucks and the general classification of driving automation. Practical verification was performed in ROS 2 and Webots for a convoy movement scenario with two vehicles.

W7223025595.title: Lightweight Visual-SLAM-Guided Autonomous Area Coverage Robot System: Design and Validation for Cluttered Indoor Environments
W7223025595.venue: WRC Symposium on Advanced Robotics and Automation (WRC SARA)
W7223025595.abstract: Achieving reliable 3D perception, autonomous navigation, and high coverage on low-cost embedded platforms remains challenging for coverage robots. This paper presents a lightweight coverage robot integrating depth-visual SLAM, ROS 2 navigation, and an improved Boustrophedon Cellular Decomposition (BCD) planner on a Raspberry Pi 5. Deploying BCD on a real visual-SLAM and Nav2 stack reveals execution failures not present in simulation: noisy maps fragment decomposition, costmap inflation blocks waypoints, and sparse path vertices cause local-planner deviation. To address these failures, application-driven BCD adaptations are presented and evaluated against three sensor configurations (visual SLAM, 2D LiDAR, fusion) and three coverage schemes. Results show that the visual SLAM configuration achieves the best tradeoff between localization accuracy, safety, and system cost. Compared with the conventional BCD implementation, the proposed adaptations reduce repetition by 18% (54.6% to 44.7%), tighten run-to-run consistency by a factor of 3.1 at negligible overhead, while the 2D LiDAR configuration collided in every trial due to an undetected low-profile obstacle.

W7223122864.title: Enumeration-Guided Training of Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Safety Certificates
W7223122864.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis offers formal safety guarantees for control systems, but training accurate neural certificates remains difficult, particularly when unsafe regions are hard to characterize. We propose a verification-guided training framework that addresses this by using probabilistic enumeration of safety constraints to detect forward-invariance violations, i.e., states where the learned certificate incorrectly classifies unsafe behavior. This produces a compact, targeted set of counterexamples that more precisely captures the failure boundary than inputs generated by standard adversarial attack methods. Crucially, using this representation to fine-tune a pretrained HJ value function yields larger certified regions and reduces certification time across all tested benchmarks. We further introduce a shielding mechanism based on the refined certificates to enforce safety constraints at deployment time. We evaluate the proposed safety filter in a realistic, physics-based Isaac Sim environment and through real-world autonomous racing experiments, achieving zero safety constraint violations compared to a nominal controller and a backup policy based on Linear Quadratic Regulation (LQR). These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed shielding mechanism in ensuring safe operation under high-speed, safety-critical conditions.

W7223471542.title: A delay-budget speed rule for pure-pursuit path tracking: model-derived operating margin and pre-specified multi-robot validation

W7223501289.title: Σχεδίαση και υλοποίηση μεθόδου καθορισμού διαδρομής για αυτόνομα οχήματα σε εικονικό περιβάλλον
W7223501289.venue: University of Thessaly Institutional Repository (University of Thessaly)
W7223501289.abstract: The development of autonomous racing vehicles presents a highly complex control and navigation challenge.Within the context of the Formula Student (FSD) competition, autonomous architectures need to balance stability and maximum performance of the vehicle.To address this dual-objective problem, this thesis formalizes the design, implementation and simulationbased validation of a comprehensive, modular autonomous architecture developed utilizing the ROS2 framework.The system employs a two-phase navigation strategy managed by a central state machine.During the initial Exploration phase, a multi-sensor fusion pipeline is integrated with an advanced GraphSLAM algorithm to detect track boundaries, estimate the current state of the vehicle and construct an accurate global map.Simultaneously, the track boundaries are extracted via Delaunay Triangulation and smoothed using B-splines, allowing computationally lightweight controllers (Pure Pursuit and PID) to safely guide the vehicle through the unmapped layout.Upon successful map closure, the architecture dynamically transitions to the Optimization phase.This phase generates the optimal racing line, smooths the optimized path and computes a dynamic velocity profile, utilizing the data from the previous phase and the physical limits of the vehicle.To execute this high-performance trajectory, a Model Predictive Controller (MPC) replaces the reactive trackers, enabling proactive limit-handling maneuvers at high velocities.The complete architecture is evaluated within the CARLA simulation environment.The results demonstrate the system's capability to execute autonomous phase transitions, while maximizing dynamic performance and vehicle stability during competitive scenarios.

W7223557019.title: Curvature-Constrained Path Planning for Skid-Steer Mobile Robots in Constrained Environments
W7223557019.abstract: This paper presents a path planning algorithm developed for a skid-steer mobile robot platform, focusing on challenges arising from non-holonomic motion constraints and limited turning capabilities. Conventional path planning methods often fail to adequately account for these kinematic constraints, resulting in sharp turns, discontinuities, and trajectories that are difficult to follow in practice. This becomes particularly problematic in narrow or complex environments, where stable and predictable motion is critical. The proposed approach aims to generate continuous, smooth, and physically feasible trajectories that minimize abrupt changes in angular velocity and improve path tracking accuracy. The algorithm combines geometric path planning with curve smoothing techniques, complemented by local correction steps that adapt to the environment and the robot’s current state. The solution is suitable for integration into real-time systems and supports autonomous navigation tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces tracking error and oscillatory behavior while improving navigation robustness. The findings highlight the importance of platform-specific path planning for reliable operation in autonomous robotic systems.

W7224102511.title: Active robot vision for mitigating worker-induced occlusion in construction monitoring

W7224447623.title: Evaluating the comfort of robot paths in varying-width corridors: passenger vs. observer perspectives
W7224447623.abstract: In corridors shared by humans and robots, mobile robots should follow paths that are comfortable for passengers and observers. Previous studies have examined straight corridors with uniform width; however, actual environments include varying-width corridors, such as hallways connected to open spaces or containing static obstacles. Comfortable path design in such environments is unclear, and differences between passenger and observer preferences remain underexplored. This study provides initial, context-specific empirical evidence on comfort preferences among robot paths in varying-width corridors from passenger and observer perspectives. Through experiments (n = 35), three paths were examined: a straight wall-following path, a center path with a small heading change, and a wall-following path with a larger heading change. Each path was evaluated in two perspectives (passenger and observer) and two environments with sudden or gradual width changes. Comfort was measured by ranking the three paths. A Plackett-Luce model was used to test within-condition path preferences, the effects of perspective and environment, and their interaction. Across all conditions, the straight wall-following path was mainly preferred. In the sudden-change environment, path preference differed significantly between perspectives: passengers preferred the center path over the path with the larger heading change, whereas observers showed no such preference and rated the latter relatively higher. No significant effect of environment or interaction was detected. These findings suggest that, within the scenarios tested, smaller heading changes are associated with comfort, whereas less center-aligned motion may be particularly relevant when observer comfort is prioritized.

W7224805711.title: Intelligent Adaptive Selection of Path Smoothing Methods and Collaborative Design of Planning and Tracking for Mobile Robots
W7224805711.venue: International Conference on Computer Engineering and Application (ICCEA)
W7224805711.abstract: Path planning and tracking control are core challenges for autonomous mobile robots operating in complex environments. To address the limitations of existing research that evaluates path quality primarily by length and time, lacking comprehensive consideration of dynamic tracking performance, and the insufficient adaptability of single smoothing methods, this paper proposes a joint optimization framework. First, improved RRT* and genetic algorithms are employed to generate initial paths. Second, the pure pursuit controller is enhanced by introducing a tangent prediction-based speed regulation strategy with a field-of-view angle constraint. Third, a multi-dimensional evaluation system encompassing path length, geometric smoothness, tracking time, tracking error, tracking smoothness, and planning time is constructed. Finally, an intelligent smoothing method selection mechanism is designed to evaluate the comprehensive performance of six smoothing algorithms (greedy, quintic polynomial, piecewise quintic polynomial, Bezier, B-spline, and enhanced Bezier) through tracking simulation, selecting the optimal path. Experimental results on five binary maps of 100×100 pixels demonstrate that RRT* outperforms genetic algorithms in comprehensive scores, achieving an average lead of 5.7%. The intelligent smoothing selection mechanism adaptively matches optimal methods according to environmental characteristics, with greedy smoothing performing best in 60% of experiments. Path smoothing effectively reduces tracking time by up to 2.9% on the maze map and improves the comprehensive score of RRT* paths by an average of 12.1%, while achieving zero sharp accelerations across all smoothed paths, significantly enhancing tracking smoothness. This study provides an effective solution for the synergistic optimization of path planning and tracking control in mobile robots.

W7225071582.title: Desenvolvimento de um robô híbrido: Caso de uso florestal
W7225071582.venue: Portuguese National Funding Agency for Science, Research and Technology (RCAAP Project by FCT)
W7225071582.abstract: A navegação autónoma em ambientes florestais apresenta desafios complexos decorrentes da natureza não estruturada do meio, da degradação de sinais de posicionamento por satélite (Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)) sob coberto arbóreo, das variações extremas de iluminação e da presença de vegetação penetrável e de obstáculos rígidos.Os robôs terrestres enfrentam limitações físicas perante desníveis e vegetação densa, enquanto as plataformas aéreas apresentam um consumo energético elevado quando comparadas com a locomoção de solo.As plataformas híbridas terrestre-aéreas surgem como uma solução promissora, combinando a eficiência energética da deslocação em solo com a capacidade de contornar obstáculos por via aérea quando o terreno se torna intransponível.Esta dissertação apresenta o desenvolvimento e validação experimental em simulação de um sistema de navegação, perceção e decisão para um robô híbrido terrestre-aéreo aplicado ao contexto florestal.A arquitetura proposta integra um pipeline de perceção multimodal (Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) e câmara) orientado ao mapeamento geométrico e semântico, distinguindo troncos, rochas, arbustos e troncos caídos da vegetação penetrável.Para garantir a estimativa contínua de pose, desenvolveu-se um sistema de Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) baseado em grafos de fatores com extração dessas quatro classes como landmarks, consolidadas ao longo do tempo (Tree-SLAM), complementado por módulos de relocalização e fecho de laço baseados em geometria relacional entre árvores.A representação do ambiente assenta numa malha de terreno 2.5D com estrutura persistente em tiles e num modelo de custo de traversabilidade contínuo.A camada de planeamento e decisão híbrida articula uma procura incremental (D * Lite) para rotas globais, um único controlador (Regulated Pure Pursuit) que acopla o seguimento de trajetória ao evitamento reativo de obstáculos em solo, um piloto automático dedicado (ArduPilot) para o controlo de voo, e um módulo de decisão responsável pela comutação entre o modo de locomoção terrestre e aéreo.Para a validação, desenvolveu-se um gerador procedimental de mundos florestais (ForestGen) com distribuição natural de povoamentos, operado em Gazebo através de uma ferramenta Command Line Interface (CLI) dedicada (forest).Os resultados obtidos mostram, entre outros, uma redução do erro de trajetória entre três e quatro vezes com a integração do Tree-SLAM face a um estimador contínuo isolado, e confirmam a fiabilidade mecânica da transição entre modos de locomoção.A validação conjunta de todas as camadas foi também realizada numa missão completa em simulação, com sucesso em três cenários distintos, uma missão em ciclo fechado, uma travessia direta de ponta a ponta e um salto aéreo desencadeado por um obstáculo real.

W7225140092.title: A data-driven modeling and estimation framework for robust vehicle motion under measurement uncertainty

W7225186795.title: Analytical Modelling and RPM Optimization of a Line Following Robot on Low-Friction Surfaces
W7225186795.abstract: In this paper, a mathematical and experimental study of RPM optimization in a line-following robot operating on low-friction surfaces using a differential-drive mechanism is presented. A traction-constrained velocity model is derived to estimate the maximum allowable speed before wheel slippage occurs during curved motion. Differential-drive kinematics along with basic friction dynamics are used to analyze the relationship between surface friction, linear velocity, and motor RPM. To observe the practical behavior of the system, a prototype robot was developed and tested on a ceramic tile surface. In addition, a Python-based simulation was carried out to study the relationship between velocity and RPM and to estimate the maximum traction limit. The results revealed a traction-limited velocity boundary that closely matched the experimental observations. The findings suggest that improved navigation performance can be achieved by operating the robot within the traction-limited stability region rather than maximizing motor speed.

W7225191523.title: Advanced artificial potential field for safe and efficient local path planning
W7225191523.venue: Industrial Robot the international journal of robotics research and application
W7225191523.abstract: Purpose This paper addresses the problem of efficient and safe local path planning for mobile robots operating in environments with unknown and randomly distributed obstacles. The purpose of this study is to develop a computationally lightweight local path planner that is designed to support obstacle avoidance, smooth goal-reaching behaviour and reliable waypoint tracking in cluttered environments. Design/methodology/approach The proposed method is developed on the basis of the artificial potential field algorithm and extends the classical formulation by incorporating future position prediction, vortex potential, a single constrained quadratic optimization problem for control signal selection and a mechanism for maintaining a safe distance from obstacles. The algorithm is evaluated in Matlab using randomly generated obstacle configurations for both the standalone local path planning problem and the waypoint tracking problem. Its performance is compared with that of selected existing local path planning methods. In addition, the proposed approach is validated experimentally using a real mobile robot. Findings The obtained results indicate that the proposed local path planner achieves low goal-reaching time, short path length, satisfactory path smoothness and accurate waypoint tracking. The method maintained repeatable obstacle-distance behaviour in the evaluated scenarios while requiring relatively low computational effort. The AAPF guidance field is used to generate a predicted trajectory, which is then checked against the proposed safety-distance criterion. Originality/value The main contribution of this work is the development of an efficient local path planning algorithm that combines safety-distance-aware obstacle avoidance, prediction-based motion planning and constrained optimization-based control signal generation within a unified framework. The proposed method offers a favourable balance between navigation performance, safety and computational complexity, which makes it suitable for real-time implementation in mobile robotic systems.

W7225275127.title: Dynamic Window Pure Pursuit for Robot Path Tracking Considering Velocity and Acceleration Constraints
W7225275127.venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems

W7225630979.title: Magic-Formula-Based Feedforward Velocity Control of a Magnetically Coupled Wall-Climbing Robot
W7225630979.abstract: This study presents a model-based feedforward method for reducing velocity errors during the vertical travel of a magnetically coupled wall-climbing robot. Permanent magnets on opposite sides of the wall maintain magnetic coupling, while a spring-preloaded linkage adjusts the drive-wheel normal force. A dedicated test bench was used to measure the traction-slip characteristics of the urethane roller-acrylic contact at normal forces of 20 and 30 N. Magic Formula models were fitted to the measurements. Representative slip magnitudes were calculated from the models and the ascent force balance using a nominal equivalent resistance of the robot. These fixed magnitudes were applied to both ascent and descent through direction-dependent wheel-velocity commands. In experiments without longitudinal velocity feedback, the compensation reduced the absolute errors in mean velocity and travel distance, averaged over all tested conditions, by approximately 76% and 69%, respectively. The method was also integrated with proportional-integral velocity feedback and pure pursuit path tracking and assessed in repeated ascent-descent trials. The results demonstrate the error-reduction capability of the fixed feedforward compensation under the tested conditions.

W7225647578.title: Heading-Sensorless Autonomous Vehicles: Luenberger-Based Linear MPC for Tracking and Safe Obstacle Avoidance
W7225647578.abstract: Following a trajectory and avoiding obstacles are two closely linked control tasks for an autonomous vehicle. Classical reactive controllers are tuned for one operating range, do not look ahead and have no built-in way to keep a minimum distance from an obstacle. This paper presents a Linear Time-Invariant Model Predictive Control (LTI-MPC) scheme combined with a Luenberger observer for the kinematic bicycle model. The model is linearised once around (0,0,0,vnom) and written in deviation coordinates so that the drift term of the predictor is exact. The observer, tuned with the discrete-time algebraic Riccati equation, rebuilds the heading from the noisy DGPS-RTK position and odometry speed, so no heading sensor is needed. Static obstacles are handled by a local re-planner with a designed clearance, and a closed-form rule links its blending length to the maximum reference heading. Tested in a closed loop with observer and measurement noise on five scenarios, the LTI-MPC reaches a tracking RMSE of 0.018 m at 4 m/s on a sinusoidal path; achieves, in simulation, a clearance of 0.98–0.99 m from the obstacle (the reference is designed for 1.0 m, the requirement is 0.5 m); and is the only controller among PID-type, Stanley and MPC whose accuracy degrades smoothly from 2 to 8 m/s with a single tuning. The observer converges within 1∘ in 0.24 s. A sweep of constant-radius turns shows that the linearisation stays accurate at up to 30∘ of heading change.

W7225732296.title: Particle Filtering with Generative Trajectory Models for State Estimation and Control
W7225732296.abstract: Generative models can support both state estimation and control in robotics. For control, a common approach is to use the model as a policy that directly samples actions conditioned on observation histories. However, models that jointly represent states, actions, and observations can also predict how the robot state and its environment evolve. We investigate whether these predictions can improve state estimation and control through a change in inference procedure, without modifying the pretrained model. To this end, we use particle filtering to maintain competing hypotheses about state histories. A single pretrained diffusion model generates these hypotheses along with their predicted observations and associated action proposals. As new measurements arrive, particles are reweighted according to how well their predicted observations match the measurements.
